The only size source, stated once per variant and identical."},"copper-speed-spelling":{"confidence":"measured","note":"The copper ports say speed 1g, the library's spelling for a copper traffic port and the one the DCIM exporter types. The ECS4530-54CSFP first spelled them 1000base-t and lost all four combo jacks from its exports for it; this variant starts from the corrected spelling."},"csfp-is-an-sfp-cage":{"confidence":"registry","note":"THE CAGES ARE SFP CAGES; CSFP IS WHAT GOES IN THEM. The Compact SFP is a module form that fits the standard SFP cage, which is the whole of its point - so the cages are std/sfp-ganged@1 (two-high stacks, the registry's 15.0 row pitch, measured here at 14.96) with media sfp and a csfp attr, the same decision the AMX3200 made for CFP2-DCO."},"figure-choice":{"confidence":"measured","note":"Gate 1. This variant's own front elevation (page 3, 1000 x 102) is cropped flush and -1.96% on aspect, the same as the base's; its rear (1000 x 101) is -0.99%, the better of the two rears. The scale is the base's, 2.273 px/mm across a 440 mm face, which three standard features confirmed there - the QSFP+ opening at 18.48 against 18.50, the RJ-45 cavity at 12.3 against 11.91 and the SFP stacks' 14.96 row pitch against the registry's 15.0 - and which this figure's own port columns agree with (see shared-shell)."},"left-end":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE DC INPUT IS ON THE FRONT, where the base has its C14: a green two-pole pluggable terminal block at x 5.7-37.8, y 12.3-29.9 - common/dc-terminal-plug-2@1, new with this device - with '- -48V~-60V = 6A Max +' printed under it, negative at the left. The ground stud beside it lands where the base's does, centre (48.6, 21.1) against (48.4, 20.7), and is drawn at the base's position. The wordmark, the name bar reading ECS4530-54CSFP-DC-I and the '(dot) SFP LED indicator' legend are as on the base."},"numbering":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"READ OFF THE ELEVATION, and each CSFP cage carries TWO numbers. Under the bottom cage of the first stack the legend reads '1' and '3'; above its top cage '2' and '4': a CSFP module presents two bidirectional fibre ports, so 24 cages give the datasheet's 48 ports - the datasheet explains that a CSFP transceiver carries two BIDI fibre ports, so each cage reaches two CPE/IAD devices and the physical port total is 48. Stack k carries 4k+1 and 4k+3 in its bottom cage and 4k+2 and 4k+4 in its top. EACH CAGE DECLARES THE TWO INTERFACES IT PRESENTS - csfp-1-3 carries `interfaces: [port-1, port-3]` (roc-ops/Portrayal#443) - so the DCIM export lists port-1..port-48 and the cages themselves are not interfaces. The switch's silicon has both ports whether or not a module is seated, which is why they belong to the cage and not to the optic. With the SFP+ as port-49..52 and the QSFP+ as port-53/54, the export is port-1..port-54 - the 54 in the model number. THE COMBO JACKS ARE copper-45..copper-48. They were port-45..48 first, which is exactly the ids the twelfth stack's CSFP interfaces need; both connectors are real and a DCIM must cable each, so the copper jacks take their own names and each carries `combo-with` its fibre interface. L105 holds interface ids apart from placement ids. Ports 45-48 are COMBO: the twelfth stack's cages and the four RJ-45s beside it are bracketed together on the faceplate, and the datasheet lists '4 RJ-45/2 CSFP' combo ports, 'Either RJ-45 or CSFP port can be chosen at a time'."},"port-lamps":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"EACH STACK'S BELLY STRIP CARRIES FOUR TRIANGLE LAMPS, down-up-down-up, which is one per logical port and says whose it is: a down-arrow points at the bottom cage and an up-arrow at the top, and each sits on the same side as that port's printed number - 1 left and 3 right below, 2 left and 4 right above. So the lamps are assigned, not guessed, by the two things the faceplate itself says about them. The SFP+ stacks carry one arrow per port the same way, and the QSFP+ stack a down-arrow, four small windows and an up-arrow; the four windows are drawn and not given to a port."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THREE FIXED FANS, BUT NOT WHERE THE BASE HAS THEM. This variant's rear elevation is the better-proportioned of the two (-0.99% on aspect against the base's +5.26%), and its three honeycomb guards centre at 119.7, 235.6 and 324.5 mm - the third 26.6 mm inboard of the base's - and run y 4.4-38.3, 40 mm wide. Different placement of the same fans on the same shell; each device carries its own."},"rj45s":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE TOP COMBO JACKS SHOW LIT LAMPS AND THE BOTTOM ONES SHOW NONE, on this variant's front as on the base's. The base's elevation draws two green windows in the upper corners of the jacks for 46 and 48, at 307.5, 318.5, 326.9 and 338.3 mm, and nothing at all in the corners of 45, 47, the console or MGMT. The top jacks are the lamped part; the rest are drawn bare because that is what the metal shows, which leaves three Ethernet jacks on a bare part and L76 standing - see the gap."},"shared-shell":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE PORT FIELD IS CARRIED FROM THE ECS4530-54CSFP AND CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. The two fronts are different artwork - registered at their best shift they still differ by 35 grey levels on average - so this is not a copy of one drawing. But the DC-I front's own openings land on the base's lattice: first CSFP column 106.7 against 105.8, last 295.9 against 295.6, the same 17.2 mm pitch, the SFP+ at 369.8 against 369.6 and the QSFP+ at 390.2 against 389.6 - within a pixel and a half everywhere. The datasheet gives both one dimension column. So the port field, lamps and legends are the base's measured ones, which were read off the better of the two front elevations; everything this note does not name was measured on this variant's own figure. ITS VERTICAL IS NOT RE-MEASURED HERE. The DC-I front's cages read lighter than the base's and the threshold catches only their interiors, so its row positions are not an independent reading; the base's are carried."},"sources":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"ONE DOCUMENT FOR TWO MACHINES. The ECS4530 Series data sheet is a two-column comparison of the ECS4530-54CSFP and this ECS4530-54CSFP-DC-I - the staged ecs4530-54csfp-i-datasheet is byte-identical - so every attr here is read from the DC-I column, not the row. There is no quick start guide. Page 3 carries both variants' fronts and both rears at 1000 px; four product photographs of this variant are staged at 489 px (1.1 px/mm), used only to say which rear is whose: its rear photograph puts the third fan at about 74% of the width, which is the rear whose guards sit at 119.7, 235.6 and 324.5 mm and not the base's (351.1). The front's name bar reads ECS4530-54CSFP-DC-I; this library names the device for the issue's ecs4530-54csfp-i."},"stack-orientation":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the port lamps, which point up over down: the 14 SFP pairs (csfp-2-4/csfp-1-3 to port-52/port-51), the 1 QSFP pair (port-54/port-53). 15 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic
